=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Harbourglass Ventures' updated positions – departures from Buyer's interests and recommended pushback

---

## 0. Threshold point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" framing

The Seller's preamble asserts the positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams," are "FINAL," and "not intended to be re-opened." Treat this as advocacy, not fact. Nothing in our instructions records any such principal-level agreement, and the Disclosure Letter's own reservation (para 11) says "no … negotiation position or approval is included." **Please confirm with the Wattlebridge principals whether anything has actually been agreed.** Unless confirmed in writing from our side, every item below remains open. We should respond that the package is received as a Seller first draft and will be marked up in full.

The "market context" paragraph is also self-serving. The ranges quoted are at the seller-friendly end; for a ~AUD 24m private SaaS share sale with real identified issues (customer concentration, undischarged debt, IP chain-of-title gap, a privacy incident), a buyer would ordinarily expect materially better protection than what is proposed.

---

## 1. Liability architecture (cl 12.1, 12.2, 12.3/13, 9.3/12.8/20.5)

### 1.1 General cap – 20% (AUD 4.8m)
Low given the risk profile. The real problem is not the number in isolation but what the Seller is trying to fold inside it (see 1.4–1.6). Recommend:
- Open at **50–100% of price** for general warranties; settle no lower than ~30–35% unless W&I insurance is in play.
- **Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances) and the Tax Indemnity: capped at 100% of price.**
- **Specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, Riverlark, bonuses, leakage) and Completion obligations: outside the cap, or on a separate cap of 100%.**

### 1.2 De minimis AUD 25,000 / basket AUD 250,000 / deductible
- AUD 25k de minimis is high for a business where many likely claims (unpaid supplier amounts, individual employee issues, single-customer disputes) sit below that. Push to **AUD 10,000**, with **aggregation of claims arising from the same or related facts** so the Seller cannot fragment a systemic issue into sub-threshold pieces.
- Basket at ~1% is acceptable as a number, but it must be a **tipping basket** (first-dollar recovery once exceeded), not a deductible ("only the excess … is recoverable"). The deductible formulation effectively reduces the price by AUD 250k on any meaningful claim.
- **No thresholds apply** to Fundamental warranties, Tax, specific indemnities, leakage/debt-free adjustments or fraud.

### 1.3 Time limits – 18 months, applied to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"
18 months for general warranties is at the short end but liveable (push for 24 months, which covers two audit cycles). The real issue is the catch-all. Reject it and specify:
- **Tax:** the later of 7 years and 3 months after Completion, or expiry of the ATO amendment period plus 3 months.
- **Fundamental warranties:** 7 years (statutory limitation under the *Limitation Act 1969* (NSW)), or at minimum 6 years.
- **Specific indemnities:** each keyed to its own subject matter (e.g. DD-006: 6 years; Ironquay: until confirmatory assignment delivered and 3 years thereafter).
- Claims notified in time survive even if proceedings are commenced later (with a reasonable 9–12 month commencement window).

### 1.4 Fundamental/title warranties under general caps and time limits
Reject outright. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to allow a 20% cap on the Seller's warranty that it actually owns the shares it is selling. If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing and the Seller's proposal would limit recovery to AUD 4.8m, subject to a basket, for 18 months. This is a non-negotiable for a buyer.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature"
Reject. Carve out expressly:
- **Fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment or wilful default** – no cap, no threshold, no time bar (in any event a contractual attempt to exclude liability for fraud is unenforceable, but we do not want to litigate the point).
- **Specific indemnities, Tax Indemnity, leakage/completion accounts adjustments, restraint and confidentiality breaches** – not subject to the warranty limitation regime.
- **Equitable and statutory remedies** – the exclusive-remedy clause must not purport to exclude liability under the *Australian Consumer Law* for misleading or deceptive conduct to the extent not excludable, nor injunctive relief for restraint/confidentiality breaches.
- The non-reliance clause should be mutual in effect and limited to representations *outside* the SPA, the Disclosure Letter and the written DD responses.

### 1.6 Seller covenant strength
Harbourglass Ventures is a venture vehicle. We have no visibility of its post-Completion asset position; it may distribute proceeds to its investors shortly after Completion. Recommend **a retention/escrow of 10–15% of price for 18–24 months** (or at least for the specific-indemnity items below), and/or a parent/fund guarantee. Alternatively price a W&I policy – but note the identified issues below (Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, Bluefen) will almost certainly be excluded from cover, so they must be solved structurally regardless.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge (Schedule 7, cl 8.3, Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.4)

### 2.1 General disclosure of the entire data room and "publicly searchable corporate records"
This is the single most buyer-adverse concept in the package, because it combines with cl 8.3 to make every warranty almost worthless. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter demonstrates the problem: it discloses the *existence* of issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006) while expressly refusing to characterise their scope, legal effect or quantum (para 1.4, para 6, para 8, para 11). A warranty "disclosed against" by a data room reference to a document the Seller says it does not interpret is not a disclosure; it is an invitation to litigate what we should have deduced.

Recommend:
- Disclosure only of matters **"fairly disclosed, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and (where reasonably practicable) the financial effect of the matter."**
- **No general disclosure of the data room.** If the Seller insists, limit to specified documents listed in a schedule, subject to the "fairly disclosed" standard.
- **Delete disclosure of public registers** entirely. ASIC/PPSR/court searches should be our tool for verifying the Seller's warranties, not a device for disclosing against them.
- Disclosure Letter para 1.4 ("nothing in this letter admits …") should be accepted only on the basis that the Buyer equally does not accept that the disclosures are adequate, and that **no disclosure qualifies the specific indemnities or Fundamental warranties.**
- Data room cut-off is 22 September 2026; today is 5 November. Require **updated disclosure only with Buyer consent**, no right to disclose new matters at Completion against the warranties, and a bring-down of warranties at Completion with a termination right for material new matters.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge qualification (cl 8.3)
Reject. As drafted it bars any claim for matters "discoverable from the data room or public records" – i.e. constructive knowledge. The Buyer should never accept a constructive-knowledge bar; it inverts the purpose of DD and rewards Seller opacity. The Buyer's maximum concession: a bar limited to **actual knowledge of two or three named Wattlebridge individuals of a specific matter, and only to the extent that matter was fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.** Do not extend to advisers. Pair with an express statement that the Buyer's DD does not limit warranty claims (a "no-investigation" clause).

---

## 3. Deal-specific issues

### 3.1 Bluefen – ~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue (cl 3/6.3; DL para 2)
The Seller's SPA note says the consent "is addressed" and will be "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." The Disclosure Letter says there is **no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met.** This is a customer-concentration deal risk going to the heart of valuation.

Recommend:
- **Condition precedent to Completion:** receipt of Bluefen's written consent under cl 11.2, **unconditional or on conditions approved by the Buyer**, with evidence that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied or waived, and confirmation Bluefen has not exercised and will not exercise any termination/renegotiation right triggered by the change of control.
- Seller obligation: **"all reasonable endeavours"** (not merely "reasonable"), with Buyer entitled to participate in communications with Bluefen.
- Buyer-only waiver and a **long-stop date** with Buyer termination right.
- Fallback if Seller resists the CP: **price adjustment or deferred consideration** tied to Bluefen revenue retention over 12–24 months, or an escrow of an amount reflecting the Bluefen revenue at risk. Also a specific warranty that no other customer contract contains a change-of-control right beyond those listed.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility – ~AUD 3.2m (cl 2/7; DL para 3)
A post-Completion release is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis and exposes the Company to default. DD-003 cl 8.1 is a change-control clause – the share sale itself will likely be an event of default permitting acceleration and enforcement of security unless the lender consents or is repaid at Completion.

Recommend:
- **Repay at Completion from the purchase price via the funds flow** (payoff letter from Riverlark delivered pre-Completion stating the exact payout figure, including break costs).
- **Completion deliverables:** executed deed of release/discharge of all security (including any charge over the shares or IP), PPSR release/financing change statements, and release of any guarantees given by the Company.
- If Riverlark holds security over the *shares*, this is also a **title issue** (see 3.9).
- Any amount not actually repaid at Completion is a price deduction, not a post-Completion promise.

### 3.3 Completion bonuses – AUD 420,000 + on-costs (DL para 5; funds flow)
The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" but they are payable **by the Company** on Completion and are not in the funds flow. Without correction, the Buyer funds them. They are transaction-triggered liabilities = debt-like items.

Recommend:
- Treat as **Transaction Expenses deducted from the price** or paid by the Seller on Completion, **grossed up for superannuation guarantee (12%), NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) and any PAYG/withholding** – realistically ~AUD 490–500k all-in.
- Itemise in the funds flow; Seller indemnity for any shortfall.
- Separately, obtain the bonus letters: confirm the continued-employment conditions and whether any have post-Completion vesting that would hit the Buyer later; check the recipients against key-person retention plans.

### 3.4 Ironquay – IP chain of title (cl 11.1; DL para 4)
DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**, and DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. Until paid, the Company does not own that IP. If SOW3 deliverables are in the product, this is a core-asset defect, not a receivable question. The Seller's indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" would compensate us for AUD 180k, not for not owning the code.

Recommend:
- **CP / Completion deliverable:** evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and a confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay** (with moral-rights consents) in favour of the Company, delivered before Completion. Seller funds the AUD 180k.
- **Broaden the indemnity** to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim in respect of, Ironquay-developed materials or any SOW, not just SOW3.
- IP warranties: full ownership of all IP in the platform, all contributors have assigned, no open-source copyleft contamination; **IP warranties on an elevated cap and extended period** (see 3.8).

### 3.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL para 6)
~1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address. The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (*Privacy Act 1988* Pt IIIC), an entity must complete its assessment of a suspected eligible data breach within **30 days**; the incident is recorded in a data room dated 22 September, so that clock has very likely run. Exposure includes OAIC regulatory action (penalties were significantly increased in 2022–2024), customer-contract breach (SaaS customers typically require incident notification within 24–72 hours), and reputational damage with Bluefen and others. Paragraph 1.4 ("does not admit … notification … is legally required") is precisely the kind of non-disclosure that cl 8.3 would otherwise turn against us.

Recommend:
- **Pre-signing information request:** full incident report, whether the recipient confirmed deletion, access logs, which customers' data is affected, whether OAIC/customers/individuals have been notified and on what basis a decision not to notify was made.
- **Specific indemnity** for all loss arising from the incident and any related regulatory action, customer claims or remediation – outside cap/basket, 6-year period.
- **Pre-Completion covenant** to complete the investigation and make any required notifications in consultation with the Buyer; **CP** that no regulator has commenced action.
- Warranties: no other actual or suspected data breaches; compliance with Privacy Act, APPs and customer data-protection obligations.

### 3.6 Office lease (DL para 7)
Likely low-risk but confirm: obtain the lease, identify the notification provision, and make delivery of the notice (and landlord acknowledgement, if any) a Completion deliverable. Confirm no change-of-control consent or bank-guarantee replacement obligation.

### 3.7 Sandbar renewals – 3 × AUD 110,000 (DL para 8)
The Seller says ordinary course; its own Disclosure Letter says it does not know whether they are "unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course." Three identical AUD 110k contracts with a related supplier, to be "read together for timing/scope," is a pattern that often reflects splitting to stay under an approval threshold.

Recommend: obtain all three contracts; confirm whether they are committed pre-Completion (then **debt-like / working-capital adjustment** to the extent prepaid or accrued), whether they are terminable, and whether Sandbar is a related party of the Seller or management. Add a **related-party warranty** and a **pre-Completion covenant** restricting new commitments > AUD 50k without Buyer consent.

### 3.8 Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
Reject. Standard buyer position:
- **Separate Tax Indemnity** (pre-Completion tax, on a AUD-for-AUD basis), 100% cap, no basket, 7-year period, plus tax warranties covering R&D tax incentive claims (common and frequently challenged for SaaS businesses), GST, payroll tax, employee share schemes, and residency.
- **IP warranties** on an elevated cap (at least 50%, given IP *is* the business) and a 3–4 year period.

### 3.9 Title (DL para 10)
A company share register is prima facie evidence only. Recommend before signing: ASIC company extract and historical extract; **PPSR search against the Company and the Seller** (any security over the shares, e.g. in favour of Riverlark?); copies of share certificates; the constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emptive rights, drag/tag); confirmation no options, convertible notes, SAFEs or employee equity exist (very common in a venture-backed SaaS company – check DD-005 in particular). **Fundamental warranties** on title, no encumbrances and no other securities, at 100% cap, 7 years, no basket.

### 3.10 Mossvale (DL para 9)
Agree the Seller's reading may be correct, but obtain the clause. If it is a pure anti-assignment clause with no change-of-control limb, no action needed beyond a specific warranty that no customer/supplier contract contains a change-of-control right other than those listed. If it has any "control" language, treat as per Bluefen (CP or notification deliverable).

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "FINAL / principal-level" framing | Not to be re-opened | Confirm internally; treat as first draft; full mark-up |
| 2 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m | Post-Completion release | Repay at Completion via funds flow; deed of release + PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables |
| 3 | Bluefen consent (30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours, "treated as satisfied" | CP: unconditional written consent + cl 11.3 satisfied; all reasonable endeavours; long-stop; fallback price adjustment/escrow |
| 4 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Payment + confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; broad IP indemnity; elevated IP warranty cap |
| 5 | Fundamental/title warranties | Same cap/time as general | 100% cap, 7 years, no basket – non-negotiable |
| 6 | General data room + public register disclosure | Everything disclosed | "Fairly disclosed" standard; scheduled documents only; no public-register disclosure; no disclosure against indemnities |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | Includes constructive/discoverable knowledge | Delete; at most actual knowledge of named individuals of fairly disclosed matters; no-investigation clause |
| 8 | Limitations apply to "all Claims" | Fraud, indemnities, tax all capped | Carve out fraud, specific indemnities, Tax, leakage, Completion obligations, ACL |
| 9 | Completion bonuses AUD 420k | Not in funds flow | Deduct from price incl. super/payroll tax (~AUD 490–500k); Seller indemnity |
| 10 | DD-006 privacy incident | "Not material" | Full disclosure now; specific indemnity outside cap; investigation/notification covenant; no-regulator-action CP |
| 11 | General cap 20% | AUD 4.8m | Open at 50–100%; floor ~30–35%; plus escrow 10–15% or parent guarantee |
| 12 | De minimis / basket | 25k / 250k deductible | 10k / 250k **tipping**; aggregation of related claims; no thresholds for Fundamental/Tax/indemnities |
| 13 | Time limits | 18 months, all claims | 24 months general; Tax 7 years; Fundamental 7 years; indemnities bespoke |
| 14 | Tax / IP | General regime | Separate Tax Indemnity (100%, 7 yrs); IP warranties elevated cap/period |
| 15 | Sandbar AUD 330k | Ordinary course | Obtain contracts; related-party check; debt-like/working-capital treatment; pre-Completion conduct covenant |
| 16 | Title verification | Share register only | ASIC/PPSR searches; constitution/SHA; no options/notes/SAFEs warranty |
| 17 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only | Obtain clauses; notice as Completion deliverable; change-of-control warranty |

**Overall:** the Seller has drafted a package in which (a) three debt-like or title-affecting items (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay) are pushed to the Buyer's side of Completion, (b) the two largest commercial risks (Bluefen, DD-006) are described but not resolved, and (c) the disclosure and knowledge mechanics would neutralise most warranty protection. Items 2–5 should be solved structurally at Completion rather than through warranty claims; items 6–8 are the drafting points that determine whether the warranty package has any value at all. I would suggest we lead the mark-up with those, and treat the headline cap/basket numbers as secondary.

I'm happy to prepare the mark-up of clauses 8.3, 9.3, 11.1, 12 and Schedule 7, and a Completion deliverables schedule, on your instruction.

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge (Schedule 7, cl 8.3, Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.4)

### 2.1 General disclosure of the entire data room and "publicly searchable corporate records"
This is the single most buyer-adverse concept in the package, because it combines with cl 8.3 to make every warranty almost worthless. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter demonstrates the problem: it discloses the *existence* of issues (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006) while expressly refusing to characterise their scope, legal effect or quantum (para 1.4, para 6, para 8, para 11). A warranty "disclosed against" by a data room reference to a document the Seller says it does not interpret is not a disclosure; it is an invitation to litigate what we should have deduced.

Recommend:
- Disclosure only of matters **"fairly disclosed, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature, scope and (where reasonably practicable) the financial effect of the matter."**
- **No general disclosure of the data room.** If the Seller insists, limit to specified documents listed in a schedule, subject to the "fairly disclosed" standard.
- **Delete disclosure of public registers** entirely. ASIC/PPSR/court searches should be our tool for verifying the Seller's warranties, not a device for disclosing against them.
- Disclosure Letter para 1.4 ("nothing in this letter admits …") should be accepted only on the basis that the Buyer equally does not accept that the disclosures are adequate, and that **no disclosure qualifies the specific indemnities or Fundamental warranties.**
- Data room cut-off is 22 September 2026; today is 5 November. Require **updated disclosure only with Buyer consent**, no right to disclose new matters at Completion against the warranties, and a bring-down of warranties at Completion with a termination right for material new matters.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge qualification (cl 8.3)
Reject. As drafted it bars any claim for matters "discoverable from the data room or public records" – i.e. constructive knowledge. The Buyer should never accept a constructive-knowledge bar; it inverts the purpose of DD and rewards Seller opacity. The Buyer's maximum concession: a bar limited to **actual knowledge of two or three named Wattlebridge individuals of a specific matter, and only to the extent that matter was fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.** Do not extend to advisers. Pair with an express statement that the Buyer's DD does not limit warranty claims (a "no-investigation" clause).

## 3. Deal-specific issues

### 3.1 Bluefen – ~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue (cl 3/6.3; DL para 2)
The Seller's SPA note says the consent "is addressed" and will be "treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." The Disclosure Letter says there is **no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met.** This is a customer-concentration deal risk going to the heart of valuation.

Recommend:
- **Condition precedent to Completion:** receipt of Bluefen's written consent under cl 11.2, **unconditional or on conditions approved by the Buyer**, with evidence that each cl 11.3 condition is satisfied or waived, and confirmation Bluefen has not exercised and will not exercise any termination/renegotiation right triggered by the change of control.
- Seller obligation: **"all reasonable endeavours"** (not merely "reasonable"), with Buyer entitled to participate in communications with Bluefen.
- Buyer-only waiver and a **long-stop date** with Buyer termination right.
- Fallback if Seller resists the CP: **price adjustment or deferred consideration** tied to Bluefen revenue retention over 12–24 months, or an escrow of an amount reflecting the Bluefen revenue at risk. Also a specific warranty that no other customer contract contains a change-of-control right beyond those listed.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility – ~AUD 3.2m (cl 2/7; DL para 3)
A post-Completion release is inconsistent with the debt-free/cash-free basis and exposes the Company to default. DD-003 cl 8.1 is a change-control clause – the share sale itself will likely be an event of default permitting acceleration and enforcement of security unless the lender consents or is repaid at Completion.

Recommend:
- **Repay at Completion from the purchase price via the funds flow** (payoff letter from Riverlark delivered pre-Completion stating the exact payout figure, including break costs).
- **Completion deliverables:** executed deed of release/discharge of all security (including any charge over the shares or IP), PPSR release/financing change statements, and release of any guarantees given by the Company.
- If Riverlark holds security over the *shares*, this is also a **title issue** (see 3.9).
- Any amount not actually repaid at Completion is a price deduction, not a post-Completion promise.

### 3.3 Completion bonuses – AUD 420,000 + on-costs (DL para 5; funds flow)
The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" but they are payable **by the Company** on Completion and are not in the funds flow. Without correction, the Buyer funds them. They are transaction-triggered liabilities = debt-like items.

Recommend:
- Treat as **Transaction Expenses deducted from the price** or paid by the Seller on Completion, **grossed up for superannuation guarantee (12%), NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) and any PAYG/withholding** – realistically ~AUD 490–500k all-in.
- Itemise in the funds flow; Seller indemnity for any shortfall.
- Separately, obtain the bonus letters: confirm the continued-employment conditions and whether any have post-Completion vesting that would hit the Buyer later; check the recipients against key-person retention plans.

### 3.4 Ironquay – IP chain of title (cl 11.1; DL para 4)
DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on **cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**, and DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. Until paid, the Company does not own that IP. If SOW3 deliverables are in the product, this is a core-asset defect, not a receivable question. The Seller's indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" would compensate us for AUD 180k, not for not owning the code.

Recommend:
- **CP / Completion deliverable:** evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and a confirmatory deed of assignment from Ironquay** (with moral-rights consents) in favour of the Company, delivered before Completion. Seller funds the AUD 180k.
- **Broaden the indemnity** to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim in respect of, Ironquay-developed materials or any SOW, not just SOW3.
- IP warranties: full ownership of all IP in the platform, all contributors have assigned, no open-source copyleft contamination; **IP warranties on an elevated cap and extended period** (see 3.8).

### 3.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL para 6)
~1,240 personal records sent to an unintended external address. The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (*Privacy Act 1988* Pt IIIC), an entity must complete its assessment of a suspected eligible data breach within **30 days**; the incident is recorded in a data room dated 22 September, so that clock has very likely run. Exposure includes OAIC regulatory action (penalties were significantly increased in 2022–2024), customer-contract breach (SaaS customers typically require incident notification within 24–72 hours), and reputational damage with Bluefen and others. Paragraph 1.4 ("does not admit … notification … is legally required") is precisely the kind of non-disclosure that cl 8.3 would otherwise turn against us.

Recommend:
- **Pre-signing information request:** full incident report, whether the recipient confirmed deletion, access logs, which customers' data is affected, whether OAIC/customers/individuals have been notified and on what basis a decision not to notify was made.
- **Specific indemnity** for all loss arising from the incident and any related regulatory action, customer claims or remediation – outside cap/basket, 6-year period.
- **Pre-Completion covenant** to complete the investigation and make any required notifications in consultation with the Buyer; **CP** that no regulator has commenced action.
- Warranties: no other actual or suspected data breaches; compliance with Privacy Act, APPs and customer data-protection obligations.

### 3.6 Office lease (DL para 7)
Likely low-risk but confirm: obtain the lease, identify the notification provision, and make delivery of the notice (and landlord acknowledgement, if any) a Completion deliverable. Confirm no change-of-control consent or bank-guarantee replacement obligation.

### 3.7 Sandbar renewals – 3 × AUD 110,000 (DL para 8)
The Seller says ordinary course; its own Disclosure Letter says it does not know whether they are "unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course." Three identical AUD 110k contracts with a related supplier, to be "read together for timing/scope," is a pattern that often reflects splitting to stay under an approval threshold.

Recommend: obtain all three contracts; confirm whether they are committed pre-Completion (then **debt-like / working-capital adjustment** to the extent prepaid or accrued), whether they are terminable, and whether Sandbar is a related party of the Seller or management. Add a **related-party warranty** and a **pre-Completion covenant** restricting new commitments > AUD 50k without Buyer consent.

### 3.8 Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"
Reject. Standard buyer position:
- **Separate Tax Indemnity** (pre-Completion tax, on a AUD-for-AUD basis), 100% cap, no basket, 7-year period, plus tax warranties covering R&D tax incentive claims (common and frequently challenged for SaaS businesses), GST, payroll tax, employee share schemes, and residency.
- **IP warranties** on an elevated cap (at least 50%, given IP *is* the business) and a 3–4 year period.

### 3.9 Title (DL para 10)
A company share register is prima facie evidence only. Recommend before signing: ASIC company extract and historical extract; **PPSR search against the Company and the Seller** (any security over the shares, e.g. in favour of Riverlark?); copies of share certificates; the constitution and any shareholders' agreement (pre-emptive rights, drag/tag); confirmation no options, convertible notes, SAFEs or employee equity exist (very common in a venture-backed SaaS company – check DD-005 in particular). **Fundamental warranties** on title, no encumbrances and no other securities, at 100% cap, 7 years, no basket.

### 3.10 Mossvale (DL para 9)
Agree the Seller's reading may be correct, but obtain the clause. If it is a pure anti-assignment clause with no change-of-control limb, no action needed beyond a specific warranty that no customer/supplier contract contains a change-of-control right other than those listed. If it has any "control" language, treat as per Bluefen (CP or notification deliverable).
